_comment: Secret shapes — the ONE rules file for catching pasted keys and credentials
before they reach inference. Read by brain/mastercode/secret_shapes.py (the
pod-side redaction in runtime/session.send_message) and by
circles-web/src/lib/secret-shapes.ts + workbench-web/src/lib/secret-shapes.ts
(the composer nudge). Both sides load THIS file; never hand-copy a pattern.
Every `pattern` must run identically under Python `re` and JavaScript `RegExp`:
no inline (?i) flags (use `flags`), no lookbehind, no named groups, no \A/\Z.
`group` (default 0) is the capture group that IS the secret — only that span
is redacted, so a URL keeps its scheme/host and an assignment keeps its name.
severity: 'hard' = unambiguous vendor/key shape. The browser warns AND the pod
redacts it before the model, the memory row, and the transcript see it.
severity: 'soft' = a heuristic (assignment, high-entropy blob). The browser
warns; the pod leaves it alone (a hash or a random id is not a leak, and
there is no user pod-side to ask).
entropy: the generic catch for key material with no vendor prefix. A token
of `min_length`+ chars from the charset that has at least one digit and one
letter and Shannon entropy >= `min_bits_per_char`. Hex-only strings (git
SHAs, hashes) top out at 4.0 bits/char and never trip a 4.3 floor; random
base64 sits at 4.6-5.2. Always soft.
keys: where the composer's 'Store in Keys' button seals a hard hit —
`name` is the vault logical name (the canonical provider name for a vendor
API key, so routing picks it up; a plain descriptive name otherwise) and
`cred_type` is api_key | opaque. Storing supersedes an existing entry of
the same name (server/vault/store.put), and the strip says so.
Messaging bot tokens (2026-10-05). Slack: app-level tokens 'begin with
xapp-', rotating ones with 'xoxe.xapp-' (docs.slack.dev/authentication/tokens);
the slack-token rule above (xox[baprs]-) never matched them. Telegram: the
Bot API docs show only an illustrative token ('123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-
zyx57W2v1u123ew11'); the rule follows the shape issued tokens have, the bot's
numeric id, a colon, and 35 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-]. It also matches
the token inside the API URL, https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getMe,
where no word boundary falls between 'bot' and the id; group 1 is the token,
so 'bot' stays. It ends on a lookahead, not \b, because a token may end
in '-'. Both seal as opaque: an api_key name must be a model provider the
router knows (scripts/test_secret_shapes.py), and a connector reads its key
by name whatever its type (nac_connector.platform_call).
A rule whose last set holds '-' ends on a lookahead, never \b: \b after a
trailing '-' needs a word character next, so a Google key ending in '-'
was missed and a JWT kept its last '-' unredacted. slack-token also covers
the xoxe- refresh, xoxe.xox?- rotating and xwfp- workflow tokens.

rules.label: value assigned to a password/secret/token field
